questions.prompt: Male part or female part of the flower?
questions.explain: Stamen = anther + filament; pistil = stigma + style + ovary.

options: The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma
The fusion of male and female cells

questions.prompt: Order the steps from flower to seed.
steps: Pollen is made in the anther
A male cell reaches the ovule
The male cell fuses with the egg (fertilisation)
The ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit

questions.prompt: A flower is small and green with feathery stigmas and lots of light pollen. How is it most likely pollinated?
questions.explain: Wind-pollinated flowers don't need bright petals or scent.

questions.prompt: What does the ovary of a flower become after fertilisation?
Plan an experiment to test whether bees are needed for mustard plants to produce seed pods.
questions.modelAnswer: Choose two groups of mustard plants of the same type and age. Cover the flowers of group A with fine mesh bags so bees can't reach them; leave group B uncovered. Keep everything else the same: soil, water, sunlight. After the flowering season, count the seed pods on each plant. If group B has many more pods, pollination by bees is important. Use several plants in each group for reliability.
rubric: Two groups: bees excluded vs allowed
questions.explain: Criterion B: design a controlled experiment.
